presentingComplaint: Sudden-onset severe breathlessness at rest for the past 45 minutes, woke from sleep gasping for air.
history: 68-year-old man with known hypertension (poorly controlled, self-reported non-adherence to antihypertensives over the past month) and known ischemic heart disease (prior NSTEMI 3 years ago, no revascularization) awoke abruptly from sleep with severe air hunger and a sensation of drowning. No preceding chest pain, fever, or cough productive of purulent sputum. He denies recent illness, diarrhea, or vomiting. He has been eating salty food at a family function over the last two days and admits missing his amlodipine and losartan doses for about a week. No history of trauma or drug ingestion. Family called emergency services immediately given his visible distress and pink frothy sputum.
examination: Acutely distressed, sitting bolt upright, unable to speak in full sentences, using accessory muscles of respiration. Drenched in sweat (diaphoretic). Cool peripheries but no cyanosis. Bilateral coarse crepitations extending from lung bases to mid-zones on auscultation. Raised JVP. S3 gallop present. No murmurs. Frothy, blood-tinged sputum noted. No peripheral pitting edema (consistent with acute flash presentation rather than chronic decompensation). Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly.
imaging: Chest X-ray: bilateral perihilar bat-wing alveolar infiltrates, upper lobe venous diversion, Kerley B lines, normal-to-mildly-enlarged cardiac silhouette
ECG: sinus tachycardia with left ventricular hypertrophy and strain pattern, no acute ST-elevation
Bedside echocardiogram: preserved-to-mildly-reduced LVEF (~45-50%), concentric LVH, no acute regional wall motion abnormality, no significant valvular lesion, no pericardial effusion
differentialDiagnoses: Acute coronary syndrome with heart failure
finalDiagnosis: Acute heart failure - flash pulmonary oedema, hypertensive (HFpEF-range LVEF, hypertensive crisis-triggered)
citations: ESC Acute and Chronic Heart Failure Guideline 2021
contraindications: Avoid high-dose intravenous fluids / aggressive volume loading
Avoid beta-blocker initiation during the acute decompensated phase
Avoid NSAIDs (worsen renal function and fluid retention)
Use nitrates cautiously if severe aortic stenosis or hypotension develops
Avoid non-selective vasodilators if concurrent significant hypotension
edgeCases: Flash pulmonary oedema with preserved EF should prompt exclusion of acute coronary ischemia and renal artery stenosis as precipitants
Severe hypoxia with rapid onset can mimic primary respiratory pathology (asthma/COPD) - bilateral crepitations plus hypertension plus S3 favour cardiogenic cause
If troponin rises further on serial testing, consider concomitant type 1 or type 2 myocardial infarction as the precipitant
